decisions.executionNote: Approach the two watches from their own sides while gradually pitching both grippers downward; initial height and object coordinates are estimated from the calibrated head image.
The initial move was rejected without execution. Use much smaller pitch and translation increments, lifting slightly to establish continuous elbow-up motion.
Continue the overhead approach toward each watch with open grippers, preserving the established joint configuration.
Finish orienting vertically and lower above the watches. Keep open while checking fingertip alignment and the link6-to-grasp offset.
Tracking stalled near a shoulder limit. Replan from measured poses using a shallower grasp angle and small forward/downward adjustments rather than forcing the discarded targets.
Correct the image-based watch approach inward and slightly back, relaxing lateral reach. Hold orientation to isolate position tracking and improve wrist-camera alignment.
Use the now-visible watches to refine overhead alignment and cautiously lower. Grippers stay open; watch height and fingertip offset remain uncertain.
Both arms resisted descent, possibly from fingertip contact. Lift slightly and square the downward orientations before any further descent or closing.
Use wrist RGB to center the raised watch bands between the jaws, correcting inward and back on both sides with a very small descent.
Finish small wrist-image alignment corrections and close on the watch bands. Retention will be checked with a lift rather than inferred from the gripper command.
Lift both closed grippers vertically to verify that the watch bands are retained and clear the toys before basket transport.
RGB shows the right watch retained but the left watch still on the table. Carry the right watch toward the blue middle basket while reopening and retrying the left grasp slightly farther back.
Continue the right transfer with smaller increments and a modestly lower carry height for reach margin. Lower the left jaws farther around the missed watch before closing.

The right forward move reached an IK boundary. Tilt the retained watch forward while lowering link6 slightly, maintaining continuity and avoiding further extension; close the left grasp at the lower band height.
No movement occurred after rejection. Reduce right orientation increments substantially to retreat continuously from the reach boundary while completing the left watch closure.
Carry the visibly retained right watch over the right half of the blue basket with a shallower wrist angle. Test the left retry by lifting; do not infer retention from its closure state.
Reduce the right carry height and reach while centering the watch inside the blue basket. The left watch remains on the table; retry farther back where its band appears in wrist RGB.
Release the retained right watch inside the middle basket and withdraw on the right. Lift the newly aligned left grasp to test retention.
The right watch is visible in blue; the left grasp was empty. Recenter over the left band and approach lower. Move the right open gripper above the rightmost wooden toy for later midline staging.
Refine the left band's lateral centering at the contact-limited height, then close gently by position. Bring the right toy body farther between the jaws, close, and begin a small retention-test lift.
Test both grasps with a controlled lift. Bring the right wooden toy toward a central staging point without crossing the arms; left watch retention is still uncertain.
Both objects are now visibly retained. Carry the left watch toward the left side of blue; lower the right toy at a clear center-front staging location for a later left-arm pickup.
Place the right-hand wooden toy onto the central-front tabletop and withdraw rightward. Continue carrying the left watch into the middle basket with reach-saving wrist tilt.
Release the second watch into blue, then retract the left arm for wooden-toy collection. Position the right open gripper above the displaced brown wooden toy without crossing the midline.
Both watches are visible in blue. Approach the leftmost white wooden toy with the left arm, and close the right jaws around the brown toy for short central staging.
The left toy tipped sideways, so re-center on its visible body before closing. Lift and shift the brown toy only to the midline for safe staging, keeping the right arm on its own side.
Carry the grasped left wooden toy toward the white basket while adding wrist tilt for reach. The brown toy was not retained; reopen and approach its larger body rather than its tapered head.
The left toy also slipped and remains on the table. Withdraw from the basket and re-approach lower with open jaws. Refine the right approach onto the brown toy's body and close before any transport.

The previous chunk executed nothing. Bridge the residual wrist-target gap with a small relaxing pitch step, then retreat toward the left toy; continue the brown-toy approach only if continuity passes.
Still no motion after the near-threshold rejection. Slightly increase only the initial relaxing pitch correction to bridge the prior accepted wrist target, then continue the cautious re-approach.
The sideways white toy's torso is left of the jaws in wrist RGB; lift slightly and center on it before another closure. Test the brown-toy grasp with a vertical lift and shift only to the midline.
Close around the now-centered white torso and lift to confirm retention. The brown toy again remained on the table, so reopen and approach lower around its body instead of assuming a grasp.
The white wooden toy is visibly retained. Lift clear of the basket rim and transport toward white with a shallower wrist angle. Close lower on the brown toy and test a short lift near the midline.

The first white toy is visibly inside the left basket. Open and route the left arm toward the staged front toy; release the brown toy at the midline and clear the right arm before left-side collection.
Lower and center the left open jaws over the staged white toy's torso, keeping the EE on the left side of the midline. Move the right arm to a separated standby position.
Make a small torso-centering correction, close the left gripper, and lift to test the staged toy grasp. Keep the right arm stationary and clear.
The second white wooden toy is visibly held. Carry it leftward and forward above the loose objects, keeping the gripper closed and gradually tilting for basket reach.
The white toy slipped during wrist tilting and is visible on the table. Re-approach its new position from above; the next carry will preserve its grasp orientation and use slower translations.
Lower onto the white toy's centered torso and close with the downward orientation unchanged. Keep the right arm clear while establishing a more secure grasp.
Lift the regrasped white toy slowly while moving away from the adjacent brown toy. Preserve the grasp orientation and check retention before continuing forward.
The toy was not retained. Re-approach lower and farther back so the pads surround the torso rather than touching only the raised base; keep the right arm clear.
The toy shifted under the approach. Lift to avoid pushing its base, recenter rightward within the left workspace and farther back over the torso, then lower straight down.
Refine using the strong wrist-image response: lift clear, shift left and slightly forward so the torso—not the head or base—is between the pads, lower, and close.
Allow the centered closure to settle, then test retention with only a slow vertical lift. Avoid rotation or sideways loading of the wooden toy.
The toy stayed fixed between the pads during the test lift. Begin a smooth leftward-forward carry, retaining the exact grasp orientation and maintaining clearance above the table.
The toy slipped near the pepper during transport. Reopen and approach its torso from the rear, clear of the pepper; the next lift will establish greater clearance before slower transport.
The white toy is now upright with its torso centered between the open jaws. Make a small rearward and downward adjustment away from the pepper, then close and settle before lifting.
Lift straight upward with the gripper closed, establishing full clearance from the neighboring pepper before any sideways carry.
Correct the malformed tensor; no motion occurred. Rotate the open left gripper above the toy to try a torso-length grasp rather than pinching its curved base.
Descend vertically with the new grasp axis and open jaws, targeting the white toy's torso while keeping clear of the peppers.
Fine-center the torso in the rotated wrist view, close along the toy's length at a lower height, and test with a short purely vertical lift.
Continue the vertical lift with the new lengthwise grasp. Verify that the toy stays between the pads rather than assuming retention from closure.
The lengthwise grasp retained the toy through the full lift. Carry it toward the white basket slowly without rotating, keeping the base above the rim and monitoring reach.
The toy remains secured. Advance over the white basket in small increments, with a slight height reduction for reach margin and no grasp rotation.

The second toy is over the white basket, but the rim disturbed tracking. Open to release and retreat from the measured pose with small reach-relaxing increments; do not force the rejected forward motion.

The released toy appears perched on the front rim rather than settled fully inside. Use a slow open-jaw forward nudge with more wrist tilt, preserving elbow continuity and avoiding extra forward arm extension.
Leave the two white toys in the left basket and approach the remaining brown wooden toy from the left. Reorient the open gripper to pinch across its narrower body while staying left of the midline.
Center the brown toy's broad carved body in the left wrist view and descend with open jaws. Stay just left of the midline and avoid gripping only the tapered head.
The carved rear body lies behind the pads. Move the left jaws rearward over that section and close; the second white toy is now outside the basket and will need a separate recovery.
Lift the closed left gripper vertically to verify the brown carved-body grasp before carrying it toward the left basket.
The brown toy was not retained; the rear-tip pinch slipped. Reopen and re-approach lower and farther forward around the wider central body instead of its rounded tail.
Use the close wrist view to center the wider shoulder/body section laterally and rearward, then close at the low grasp height and allow the grasp to settle.
Test the low central-body grasp with a slow vertical lift, keeping both position-controlled jaws closed and the other arm clear.
The brown toy remains fixed in the jaws through the lift. Raise farther and move left behind the peppers, establishing clearance before turning toward the white basket.
The brown toy remains held after rotating within the jaws. Move toward white while gradually tilting forward to place the hanging body beyond the front rim without extending the arm fully.
Shift the retained brown toy fully beyond the white basket's front rim by a small forward move and gradual wrist tilt; keep holding until its release position is visually confirmed.
Release the brown toy over the interior of the white basket, then withdraw behind its rim. The white toy on the tabletop in front will be recovered separately.
The brown toy is inside white. Approach the fallen white toy just in front of the basket, restoring a vertical lengthwise grasp while lowering with the jaws open.
The basket wall partly occludes the wrist view. Use the head alignment for a low lengthwise closure on the white toy, then lift vertically before approaching the rim again.
The grasp was empty and the white toy shifted. Recenter slightly right and forward on its visible torso, reopen and descend, then close for another short lift test.
The white toy was displaced by the rim contact. Clear the nearby peppers first: approach the left pepper with fore-aft jaw spacing and bring the right arm to a separated midline receiving standby.
Center the left pepper in the rotated wrist view and lower around its sides, keeping the jaws oriented away from the neighboring pepper. Close only after the approach.
Lift the left pepper vertically to check that it is retained before staging it for the right arm; keep the receiving arm separated.
The pepper is visibly retained. Carry it to a clear midline-front staging spot without crossing the left EE into the right workspace; move the right arm aside to prevent gripper interference.
Lower the pepper onto the clear midline-front tabletop, release, and withdraw the left gripper. Bring the right arm only to a separated approach position, not into the releasing gripper.
Approach the staged pepper from the right, stopping the right EE on its own side of the midline. Move the left arm back toward the remaining pepper, with the grippers separated fore-aft.

Center and close on the second pepper with the left gripper. The staged pepper is left of the right pads; lift and angle the right fingers slightly inward while keeping its EE on the right, then lower again.
Lift the second pepper away from the adjacent toy with the left arm. The right wrist view now shows the staged pepper between the open pads; make a small centering descent and close.
The second pepper stayed on the table; reopen and re-center its body from the latest wrist image. Test the right grasp with a lift, then move slightly rightward away from the staging area.

The right pepper was not retained. Re-approach it farther back and lower with the inward tilt preserved. Recenter the left pepper between the rotated pads and close, keeping the two approaches separated.
Make small wrist-image centering corrections on both peppers and close at the low grasp height. Retention is still unconfirmed; avoid transport until a vertical lift check.
